title: Predicting the severity of COVID-19 using machine learning methods.
summary: Among 816 hospitalized patients in one Iranian province, retrospective models classified COVID-19 severity from blood tests; random forest and XGBoost reached AUCs of 0.91 and 0.90, with D-dimer a strong predictor.
ai_technology: Support vector machine, least-squares support vector machine, random forest and XGBoost models classified COVID-19 severity from routine blood-test records.

evidence.tested: A retrospective study of 816 hospitalized patients in Hamadan Province used WHO-based severe/non-severe labels. Random forest and XGBoost AUCs were 0.91 and 0.90, with mean sensitivities of 76% and at least 74%; D-dimer was a leading predictor.
evidence.unknown: The study is a retrospective classification from one province. External validation, prospective clinical performance and benefit from model-guided care are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Support vector machine, least-squares support vector machine, random forest and XGBoost models classified COVID-19 severity from routine blood-test records.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
